## TL;DR

Added `repoos restart` so one command restarts this repo’s control-plane server whether it runs under `repoos service`, as a hand-run `repoos serve`, or under an external supervisor such as a hand-written launchd plist with `KeepAlive`. The command locates the server via the serve lockfile and `~/.repoos/servers/`, prints which path it took, warns when engineers were active, and succeeds only after `/api/health` answers with a new pid and version. `repoos status` now points stale-server warnings at `repoos restart`.

## Work and rationale

The Kamrai incident showed three gaps: `repoos service restart` only sees RepoOS-managed units, `repoos status` suggested `repoos serve` for a supervised daemon, and the documented `sudo launchctl kickstart` path failed for a non-sudo user. The fix keeps `repoos service` semantics intact (#0185) and reuses its `restartService` for managed installs while adding detection for external launchd/systemd jobs via `launchctl print pid/<pid>` and `systemctl status`.

Server discovery follows the same sources as `repoos stop` and status: live serve locks in `.repoos/` plus validated entries in `~/.repoos/servers/`, always canonicalized by repo root so another project’s listener is never touched. Restart paths are explicit in output (`managed-service`, `external-supervisor`, `hand-run`). Externally supervised restarts only `SIGTERM` the exact recorded pid—never `pkill`—and wait for the supervisor to respawn; hand-run stops then spawns a detached `repoos serve` with the same port and host from the lock.

Success waits on `/api/health` and a pid change, reporting old and new pid and version. Failure modes include supervisor timeout (prints the derived manual command, e.g. `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/…`) and refusal when the pid is owned by another user without automatic sudo. Active engineer count comes from `/api/health` so users are told agents were running; in-process adoption after a real server start remains #0214’s responsibility.

`restartHint` in `repoos status` is always `repoos restart`, since the new command subsumes the old per-mode hints. User docs in `user-docs/cli.md` and `user-docs/troubleshooting.md` were updated accordingly. No new HTTP API was added; `POST /api/server/restart` remains the in-process reload hook.

## Approaches tried

Centralizing logic in `src/core/server-restart.ts` with injectable dependencies kept CLI thin and made table-driven tests practical for managed, supervised, hand-run, timeout, and other-user refusal without spawning real servers. Supervisor detection intentionally ignores `com.repoos.serve.*` labels so RepoOS-managed services stay on the managed path even if launchctl can see the job.

## Challenges and blockers

ESM same-module mocking does not intercept internal `detectExternalSupervisor` calls from `classifyRestartPath`, so classification of external supervision is covered via `restartRepoServer` injection and `parseLaunchctlPidPrint` parsing tests rather than spying on the classifier. A human with a real LaunchDaemon on macOS should still smoke-test respawn timing; this run did not execute that hardware proof.

## Key learnings

The serve lockfile remains the authoritative pid for reload orphans (#0185 reap pattern); registry entries enrich version display and cross-check health but locks lead when alive. Restart is a full process recycle for hand-run and external supervisor paths, so agent adoption on boot is the right #0214 hook—`repoos restart` warns but does not block when engineers are active. Keeping managed and external paths separate avoids changing `repoos service` while still covering hand-written plists RepoOS did not install.
